newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HTCC SEES EXPANSION OF LINES IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: HTCC SEES EXPANSION OF LINES IN HUNGARY.

text.p: The Hungarian Telephone and Cable Corp (HTCC) said on Tuesday it planned to boost the number of access lines it operated in Hungary to some 150,000 by the end of 1997 from 85,000 at end November 1996.
HTCC has operated five local telephone concessions in Hungary since 1995.

Despite the addition of an average 1,500 new access lines a month this year, HTCC's waiting list remained static, with some 60,000 new orders, HTCC Chairman and CEO James G. Morrison told a news conference.
He said that HTCC had completed its financial arrangements for planned dynamic development and business expansion in its operation regions.
Morrison added that HTCC was also looking for expanding into other local concessions in Hungary.
He said that according to his information, Hungarian telecommunications company Matav which is majority owned by Deutsche Telekom and Ameritech, did not want to sell any of its local concessions.
"We have been in discussion with other independent local telephone operators about potential merger, acqusition," he added.
Morrison told Reuters that HTCC was also looking at local telephone concessions in other Central eastern European countries as potential expansion area.
"We are looking at opportunities in the Czech Republic and Poland currently," he said. "This is the very early phase."
HTCC has invested almost $200 million in Hungary and the amount is een increasing to $260 million by the end of 1997 when the company plans to finish its investments programme.
